title: Ashwin Warns Kohli Must 'Stay on Top' After Selectors Move to Drop Rohit Sharma
excerpt: The veteran spinner says no player's position is safe as India fast-track their transition for the 2027 World Cup, and calls for senior players to be 'shown the path with dignity.'
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ashwin warns Kohli must maintain peak performance to secure his place in the team.
  • Selectors plan to transition to younger players ahead of the 2027 World Cup.
  • Kohli scored 310 runs in his last five ODIs, averaging 62.
  • Ashwin emphasizes the need for dignified communication when dropping senior players.

Ravichandran Ashwin has issued a pointed warning about the future of Indian cricket's biggest names, saying Virat Kohli must remain at the peak of his game to avoid the same fate reportedly being handed to Rohit Sharma by India's selectors.

Speaking on his YouTube channel after India's ongoing ODI series against England, the veteran spinner said no player's position can be considered safe in the current environment — not even Kohli's.

A Warning for Kohli

"The way this is going, Virat Kohli also has to be on top of his game, unfortunately," Ashwin said. "He's batting beautifully. I've never seen Virat bat like this. I'd love to have him in the squad in South Africa, but he has to stay on top of it."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=NI6vrGhnEVw

The remarks followed reports in The Indian Express that the Ajit Agarkar-led selection committee has informed Rohit Sharma that the BCCI wants to back younger opening options, including Yashasvi Jaiswal, ahead of the 2027 World Cup in South Africa. Rohit scored 37 runs in two ODIs against England at an average of 18.50 before the third match at Lord's.

Ashwin acknowledged the complexity of the situation. "I don't know, I hope it's not the case, but seriously, Rohit hasn't been too bad either," he said.

> **"If someone is dropped, there's no problem with that," Ashwin said."**

"If someone is dropped, there's no problem with that," Ashwin said."

'Show Them the Path With Dignity'

Beyond the question of who stays and who goes, Ashwin's most striking comments were about how the process should be handled. He drew a parallel between corporate departures and the treatment of iconic cricketers.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DaKVxFPqK9V/

"If someone has performed for two decades for the country, achieved so much, at least talk to them properly, show them the path with dignity."

— Ravichandran Ashwin

"Anyone can be dropped — that's the selector, captain, and coach's job. If someone is dropped, there's no problem with that," Ashwin said. "My point is, there should be a direct communication channel, done properly."

He compared it to how large corporations handle senior layoffs: "When someone at a senior level who has contributed a lot to the company is let go, they should have a proper conversation."

Kohli returned to the England series after missing a three-match home ODI stint due to a hamstring injury. He was dismissed for five in the opening game but bounced back with 65 off 66 deliveries in the second ODI in Cardiff. Over his last five ODIs, Kohli has scored 310 runs at an average of 62 with a strike rate of 103.33, including one century and two half-centuries.

https://x.com/ManojTiwariIND/status/2079179485354799498

But Ashwin's comments suggest that even this level of performance may not provide a permanent shield as India accelerate their transition toward a younger squad for 2027.

A Generational Transition

The discussion around Rohit and Kohli reflects a broader inflection point for Indian cricket. Both batters retired from Test cricket in 2025, and the white-ball transition has been underway with players like Jaiswal, Shubman Gill, and Abhishek Sharma taking on larger roles.

For the millions of Indian cricket fans worldwide — including the diaspora, for whom Kohli and Rohit remain the most recognized sporting figures — the prospect of watching the team without its two most iconic players represents the end of an era. Ashwin's intervention adds a layer of authority to the conversation, coming from a peer who shared the dressing room with both for over a decade.

Looking Ahead

Transitioning Indian Cricket
›Selectors back younger players like Yashasvi Jaiswal.
›Rohit Sharma's average: 18.50 in recent ODIs.
›Kohli and Rohit retired from Test cricket in 2025.
›Emerging players include Shubman Gill and Abhishek Sharma.

India are expected to finalize their 2027 World Cup planning in the coming months. The selectors' handling of Rohit — and whether Kohli receives similar treatment if his form dips — will set a precedent for how Indian cricket manages its most celebrated players during periods of transition.
